rounds.text: Supreme Infrastructure India Ltd trades at an astonishing price-to-earnings ratio of just 0.14x, representing a massive valuation discount compared to the sector benchmark of 14.88x [E5]. Furthermore, the company generates an extraordinary return on assets of 228.26%, utterly dwarfing the sector benchmark of 2.8% [E7]. Operational momentum has turned dramatically positive, evidenced by a dramatic acceleration in trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth to 70% [E14], alongside screening signals confirming year-over-year sales surges exceeding 200% [E61] and robust profit growth surpassing 20% [E64]. This fundamental inflection means profit growth now exceeds one-year price growth by 102%, signalling that the business is actively beginning to outperform market expectations [E50]. Conceded: the company has delivered a poor compounded sales growth of -24.3% over the past five years [E56], alongside a negative return on equity of -286.56% [E8] and a zero dividend yield [E3].

Supreme Infrastructure India Ltd carries deep structural risks that completely undermine any superficial valuation optimism. The company has delivered a disastrous compounded sales growth of -26% over 10 years, -24% over 5 years, and -12% over 3 years, highlighting a severe, long-term erosion of its core business [E11, E12, E13, E56]. This multi-year top-line collapse sits in stark contrast to the sector median sales growth of 7.5% [E68]. Furthermore, the company exhibits a catastrophic return on equity of -286.56%, which wildly underperforms the sector benchmark of 9.37% and points to extreme shareholder value destruction [E8]. Compounding these profitability and growth failures, the stock offers a dividend yield of 0.00% [E3]. On valuation, the price-to-book ratio sits at an elevated 3.63x compared to a sector benchmark of 1.33x, meaning investors are paying a hefty premium for a deteriorating asset base [E6]. Conceded: the company displays a TTM compounded sales growth of 70% alongside a very low P/E of 0.14x and a high ROA of 228.26% [E5, E7, E14].

Conceded: long-term compounded sales growth over 10, 5, and 3 years is negative at -26%, -24%, and -12% [E11, E12, E13, E56]. However, the bear entirely dismisses the massive operational turnaround demonstrated by a trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth of 70%, which heavily outperforms the sector median sales growth of 7.5% [E14, E68]. This sudden acceleration has triggered screens for strong sales growth and year-over-year surges exceeding 200% [E61, E62]. While the bear points to a negative ROE, it ignores the extraordinary asset efficiency shown by an ROA of 228.26% against a sector benchmark of 2.8% [E7, E8]. Furthermore, the bear's complaint about a high P/B ratio ignores the staggering counter-evidence of a P/E ratio of just 0.14x, which sits miles below the sector benchmark of 14.88x [E5, E6]. Finally, the bear's criticism of dividend yield overlooks that profit growth is currently exceeding 1-year price growth by 102%, marking an inflection point where the company is starting to outperform expectations [E3, E50].

The bull’s reliance on a 70% trailing twelve-month sales growth [E14] ignores the structural decay evidenced by the 10-year, 5-year, and 3-year compounded sales growth figures of -26%, -24%, and -12% respectively [E11, E12, E13, E56]. Conceded: the company has shown a recent surge in sales [E61, E62] and profit growth [E64], but this must be weighed against a catastrophic ROE of -286.56% [E8]. While the bull highlights an ROA of 228.26% [E7], this figure is mathematically irreconcilable with the deeply negative ROE, suggesting severe balance sheet instability rather than operational efficiency. Furthermore, the P/B ratio of 3.63x is significantly higher than the sector benchmark of 1.33x [E6], indicating that the market is already pricing in a premium that the long-term sales decline does not justify [E11, E12]. Finally, the lack of any dividend yield [E3] provides no cushion for investors while they wait to see if the recent "inflection point" [E50] can actually reverse a decade of negative growth [E11].
